newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - December 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - December 12.

text.p: stories reported in the Irish press on Thursday.

- Dunnes stores is likely to be asked to hand over further documents in addition to the Price Waterhouse report to help the investigation now under way into payments made by the company to politicians.
- New proposals to fund politics and make the disclosure of all significant financial contributions mandatory were approved by the government on Wednesday.
- The former minister for Transport, Energy and Communications, Michael Lowry, is to make his long-awaited personal statement to parliament on Thursday following his resignation two weeks ago.
- A credible IRA ceasefire could mean Sinn Fein joining the multi-party talks on the North by the end of next January, Irish Prime Minister John Bruton said on Wednesday.
- Irish-American multi-millionaire businessman Chuck Feeney is the principal donor to Sinn Fein's U.S. operation but has denied that the money comes from his General Atlantic Group.
- The cabinet has given approval for grant aid for up to 4,000 jobs including an IBM project in Dublin which will provide up to 3,000 jobs.
- The opposition Fianna Fail has acused the Irish government of grossly mismanaging the public finances.
- The Irish central bank has warned that there is very limited scope for tax cuts in the January budget.
- The IRA has compiled a huge intelligence dossier on police and military personnel including names, addresses and personal details.
- Tax payers will have to pay 6.5 million Irish pounds over the next five years to fund political parties.
- College gradutates are enjoying the best job prospects for years and their unemployment rate has dropped to its lowest level since the late 1980s.
- Some 31 hospitals were checking their records on Wednesday night to see if they had received 12 "issues" of suspected HIV blood from the Blood Transfusion Service Board.
- More than 70 government leaders from every corner of Europe converge on Dublin on Thursday evening for a two-day EU summit.
- Trade unions at the state run Telecom Eireann have offered to pay approximately 90 million Irish pounds to buy a 10 percent shareholding.
